title: Pangram
statement: Given a sentence, return true if it contains every English letter at least once.
think: What is the task asking? Given a sentence, return true if it contains every English letter at least once.
What is the key operation? Identify the repeated action over the input.
What wording signals stand out? all letters, 26 unique letters, seen letters.
What is the brute force idea? Use extra loops or repeated checks.
What is the better/optimal idea? Use a clean hashset solution.
What are the edge cases? Empty-like input, single values, duplicates, and boundaries.
What is the complexity? For most of these easy tasks, aim for O(n) time unless sorting is required.
How would I explain it in an interview? State the pattern, the key operation, and the complexity.
interview: I would solve it using HashSet. I would first identify the core operation, then apply a simple hashset approach and mention the complexity.
ru: Если нужно собрать все буквы алфавита, set — естественный выбор.
visualExplanation: Walk through the input step by step and update the state after each element or window.

critical: Choose the wrong pattern instead of HashSet
important: Forget one key edge case or condition
nice: Do not explain the complexity or trade-off clearly

gaps: Important: recognize when this is a HashSet problem
Nice to have: explain why a simpler but slower brute-force approach is worse
examples: "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog" -> true
whyThisPattern: This is a HashSet problem because the wording signals are: all letters, 26 unique letters.
whyNotOtherPatterns: Not Dictionary, because we only need seen/not-seen behavior.
Not Two Pointers, because there is no two-end traversal or in-place rewrite.
